title_en: Zhang Jianming v. Jinglong Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. — dispute over payment of compensation
ruling_gist_en: The rules and regulations of an employer are internal systems implemented within the enterprise concerning the organization of labor processes and labor management. Where an employer terminates a labor contract on the ground that the worker has seriously violated the employer's rules and regulations, and the worker initiates related litigation, the court shall review the legality and reasonableness of such rules and regulations in accordance with the law. If the employer's rules and regulations exceed reasonable authority by imposing obligations on workers and the labor contract is terminated on that basis, such termination constitutes an illegal termination, harming the lawful rights and interests of the worker, and the employer shall pay compensation in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Zhang Jianming v. Jinglong Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Payment of Compensation

【Ruling Summary】

The rules and regulations of an employer are internal rules implemented within the enterprise, concerning the organization of the labor process and the conduct of labor management. Where an employer terminates a labor contract on the grounds that a worker has seriously violated the employer's rules and regulations, and the worker files a related lawsuit, the court shall, in accordance with the law, examine the legality and reasonableness of such rules and regulations. If the employer's rules and regulations impose obligations on workers beyond reasonable limits, and the labor contract is terminated on that basis, such termination constitutes an illegal termination, harming the lawful rights and interests of the worker, and the employer shall pay compensation in accordance with the law.

Plaintiff: Zhang Jianming, male, 29 years old, residing in Suzhou, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Jinglong Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd., domiciled at Fengli Street, Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Zhang Jianming, filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Suzhou Industrial Park, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Jinglong Technology (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinglong Company), regarding a dispute over the payment of compensation.

Plaintiff Zhang Jianming alleged: The plaintiff commenced employment with the defendant Jinglong Company on November 5, 2007, and signed a labor contract with Jinglong Company on December 26, 2007, with the contract term from December 26, 2007, to December 6, 2010. After the contract was signed, the plaintiff performed his job duties in accordance with the agreement. On April 20, 2009, Jinglong Company notified the plaintiff of the termination of the labor contract on the grounds that the plaintiff had taken an illegal passenger vehicle. The plaintiff believed that Jinglong Company's act of terminating the labor contract lacked factual and legal basis and constituted an illegal termination of the labor contract. The plaintiff applied for arbitration, and the arbitration award rejected the plaintiff's claims. To protect his lawful rights and interests, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit, requesting the court to order the defendant to pay economic compensation of RMB 7,800 and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant Jinglong Company argued: At approximately 10:30 a.m. on April 13, 2009, the plaintiff Zhang Jianming was discovered by the security guards of the company's dormitory area while taking an illegal passenger vehicle to the dormitory area. The security guards immediately made a record based on relevant regulations and reported the matter to the supervisor. After repeated verification and clarification of the incident, the company immediately decided to treat it as a disciplinary violation resulting in termination of the labor contract and notified Zhang Jianming to complete the corresponding resignation procedures. Because Zhang Jianming did not come to complete the resignation procedures, the company's human resources department issued a "Resignation Notice" on April 20 and completed the subsequent resignation and employment termination filing procedures. The company did not violate the provisions of the Labor Contract Law and therefore is not required to pay compensation. The company requested that the plaintiff's claims be dismissed.

The People's Court of Suzhou Industrial Park found in the first instance:

The plaintiff, Zhang Jianming, commenced employment with the defendant Jinglong Company on November 5, 2007, and signed a labor contract with Jinglong Company on December 26, 2007, with the contract term from December 26, 2007, to December 6, 2010. It was agreed that Zhang Jianming would work as an equipment maintenance engineer, with a monthly salary of RMB 2,542. At approximately 10:00 a.m. on April 13, 2009, Zhang Jianming took a vehicle with license plate number Su E8D891 to the dormitory area of Jinglong Company. On April 20, 2009, Jinglong Company issued a resignation notice to Zhang Jianming, terminating the labor contract with Zhang Jianming on the grounds that he had taken an illegal passenger vehicle.

On September 8, 2008, the defendant Jinglong Company held a职工代表大会 (workers' congress) and passed a resolution stating "Illegal passenger vehicles are not allowed to be taken; violators shall be dismissed." It was confirmed by both parties that April 13, 2009, was the plaintiff Zhang Jianming's day off. Zhang Jianming's average monthly salary for the twelve months prior to his resignation was RMB 2,600. On June 2009, Zhang Jianming submitted his claims in this case to the Labor Dispute Arbitration Commission of Suzhou Industrial Park for arbitration. The arbitration commission issued an award on July 27, 2009, rejecting all of Zhang Jianming's arbitration requests.

The focus of dispute in the first instance of this case was: Whether the defendant Jinglong Company's termination of the labor contract with the plaintiff Zhang Jianming had a legal basis.

The People's Court of Suzhou Industrial Park held in the first instance:

An employer's rules and regulations are rules and systems formulated by the employer for organizing the labor process and conducting labor management, also known as internal labor rules. The rules and regulations must comply not only with the provisions of laws and regulations but also be reasonable. The defendant Jinglong Company has the right to manage normal production and business activities by formulating rules and regulations. However, for conduct of workers outside the scope of the labor process and labor management, it is appropriate for the employer to make advocacy provisions—employees who comply may be rewarded, but it is not appropriate to make prohibitive provisions, let alone punish employees who violate such provisions. Jinglong Company, on the grounds that taking illegal passenger vehicles poses a potential risk of work-related injury, stipulated that employees are not allowed to take illegal passenger vehicles, and violators would be dismissed. This provision has exceeded the scope of internal enterprise labor rules. Moreover, the act of taking illegal passenger vehicles should be managed by administrative authorities in accordance with laws or regulations; the employer has no right to deal with such conduct. Work-related injury identification is an administrative act, and the liability for work-related injury compensation is a statutory liability borne by the employer. Jinglong Company's attempt to exclude work-related injury liability through the establishment of rules and regulations has no legal basis and is therefore also invalid. Accordingly, Jinglong Company could not base its action against the employee on this provision. The company's termination of the labor contract on the grounds that the plaintiff Zhang Jianming had taken an illegal passenger vehicle violated the provisions of the Labor Contract Law, harmed the lawful rights and interests of the worker, and should pay compensation to Zhang Jianming in accordance with the law. Zhang Jianming's request for Jinglong Company to pay compensation of RMB 7,800 did not exceed the scope of compensation prescribed by law, and the court supported it.

Based on this, the People's Court of Suzhou Industrial Park, in accordance with Articles 48 and 87 of the Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on November 19, 2009:

The defendant Jinglong Company shall pay the plaintiff Zhang Jianming compensation of RMB 7,800 within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect.

Jinglong Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed an appeal with the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, arguing: The company's formulated rules and regulations did not exceed the scope of the labor process and labor management, and dealing with the employee, the appellee Zhang Jianming, based on these rules was not improper; the company was not using the rule "Illegal passenger vehicles are strictly prohibited; violators shall be dismissed" to exclude work-related injury.

The appellee Zhang Jianming responded: The first-instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law; Zhang Jianming took the illegal passenger vehicle during his rest time, not during working hours. Therefore, he requested that the first-instance judgment be affirmed and the appeal be dismissed.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, after the second instance, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The focus of dispute in the second instance of this case was: Whether the appellant Jinglong Company's termination of the labor contract with the appellee Zhang Jianming based on the company rule "Illegal passenger vehicles are strictly prohibited; violators shall be dismissed" was lawful.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

An employer's rules and regulations refer to the rules and systems formulated by the employer in accordance with the law, implemented only within the enterprise, concerning how to organize the labor process and conduct labor management. They are behavioral norms for both the employer and the worker during the labor process, also known as internal labor rules. Their content mainly includes labor contract management, wage management, social insurance, welfare benefits, working hours and leave, employee rewards and punishments, and other labor management matters. As a management tool for employers to strengthen internal labor management, stabilize and coordinate labor relations, and ensure normal labor production order, rules and regulations indeed play an important role in daily labor order. However, rules and regulations must not only comply with the provisions of laws and regulations but also be reasonable and fair; they cannot be infinitely expanded or exceed the scope of the labor process and labor management. In this case, the day when the appellee Zhang Jianming took the illegal passenger vehicle happened to be his day off. A worker has the right to control his own conduct, and the company cannot use rules and regulations formulated for production and operation periods to restrict an employee's conduct during rest time. What means of transportation an employee uses to commute to work is the employee's private matter, and the employer has no right to make compulsory provisions. If the worker has indeed violated the law, it should be dealt with by state administrative authorities or other competent bodies. Therefore, the appellee Jinglong Company's termination of the labor contract because Zhang Jianming took an illegal passenger vehicle constituted an illegal termination, harming the worker's lawful rights and interests. It must pay compensation to Zhang Jianming in accordance with the provisions of the Labor Contract Law.

In summary, the appellant Jinglong Company's grounds for appeal could not be sustained; the first-instance judgment was not improper and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on March 25, 2010:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
